newsitem.title: UK: Regan gets extension to court order in CWS battle.
newsitem.headline: Regan gets extension to court order in CWS battle.

text.p: Andrew Regan, the entrepreneur masterminding a takeover of Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS), has been granted an extra 18 hours to prepare an affidavit by a London court, his spokesman said on Tuesday.

"He has been given an 18-hour extension to submit affidavits," the spokesman told Reuters, adding Regan had also replied to a letter from CWS chief executive Graham Melmoth. Regan's audacious plan to buy the 153-year-old CWS was thwarted last week when the Co-op obtained an order preventing him from using any confidential information.
The court order followed the suspension last week of two senior CWS executives, Allan Green and David Chambers, for an alleged serious breach of trust.

The order prohibited Regan, his company Lanica, an offshoot company Galileo, Lanica director and former CWS adviser David Lyons and Green from using any confidential material they may have about the CWS.

Regan has written to CWS chairman Melmoth in reply to questions about an earlier deal bewteen CWS and Hobson, a company then run by Regan. In the letter he said a payment queried by Melmoth formed part of a legitimate transaction which had been in the best interests of Hobson.

Regan's Galileo was last week about to bid over one billion pounds for the non-retail parts CWS which include the profitable Co-operative Bank with the intention of breaking the business up. Buyers have already emerged for some of the businesses.
